identity.title: The Relationships between Active Galactic Nucleus Power and Molecular Gas Mass within 500 pc of the Center of Elliptical Galaxies

paper_type_evidence.quote: We examine CO line emission from cold molecular gas in elliptical galaxies using archival ALMA observations to investigate the correlation between cold gas mass and AGN power.

evidence.quote: We also add M 87, which is a BCG not examined in Paper I.

targets.name: 9 BCGs from Paper I (NGC 5044, Centaurus, Abell 262, Abell 3581, Abell 2052, 2A0335+096, Hydra A, Abell 1795, PKS 0745-191)

evidence.quote: for 9 brightest cluster galaxies (BCGs) at the center of clusters (cite: 2023arXiv230316927F)

question.value: Which physical quantity controls AGN feedback in elliptical galaxies: how does molecular gas mass within 500 pc of the center relate to AGN jet power, continuum luminosity and black hole mass, and does the P_cav-M_mol relation extend from BCGs to non-central ellipticals?

evidence.quote: The physical quantity that directly controls the feedback of active galactic nuclei (AGNs) in elliptical galaxies remains to be determined.
We investigate whether the $P_{\rm cav}$–$M_{\rm mol}$ scaling relation is continuous from less massive NCEGs to giant elliptical galaxies (BCGs).

claims.hypothesis: Molecular gas mass within 500 pc scales with AGN jet power across NCEGs and BCGs
claims.experiment: Kendall correlation and censored power-law regression of P_cav vs M_mol for 22 galaxies
claims.finding: AGN jet power depends on circumnuclear molecular gas mass

evidence.quote: We find that the mass ($M_{\rm mol} \sim 10^5$–$10^9\rm\: M_\ensuremath{\odot}$) is correlated with the jet power of their AGNs

claims.hypothesis: The P_cav-M_mol relation extends to the lower-mass non-central ellipticals
claims.experiment: Correlation test restricted to the 12 NCEGs
claims.result: No correlation among NCEGs alone; the correlation is driven by BCGs
claims.finding: Not clear whether the relation extends from BCGs to NCEGs; more samples needed

evidence.quote: Note that the correlation is mainly influenced by the BCGs.
Thus, it is not clear whether the $P_{\rm cav}$–$M_{\rm mol}$ relationship extends from the BCGs to the NCEGs.

claims.hypothesis: M_mol correlates with short-timescale AGN continuum luminosities at 1.4 GHz and 100-300 GHz
claims.experiment: Kendall correlation of L_con and L_1.4 with M_mol over the extended sample
claims.finding: AGN activity depends on gas amount regardless of timescale; Paper I's null result was due to small sample

evidence.quote: The results of the current paper suggest that the lack of correlations is simply due to the small number of sample galaxies and the narrow range of $M_{\rm mol}$.

claims.hypothesis: Black hole mass, rather than gas mass, controls AGN jet power
claims.experiment: Kendall correlation of M_BH with P_cav for 22 galaxies
claims.finding: No conclusive evidence M_BH is a primary factor; M_mol is likely the main factor

evidence.quote: Thus, there is no conclusive evidence that the mass of a black hole is a primary factor in the activity of an AGN, at least within our sample of galaxies.

claims.hypothesis: The 100-300 GHz AGN continuum is mostly synchrotron rather than dust
claims.experiment: F_con/F_1.4 ratios plus a power-law + modified blackbody SED comparison
claims.result: Ratio below one except NGC 5044; dust effect minimal at 100-300 GHz
claims.finding: Continuum from ~1.4-300 GHz is mostly synchrotron

evidence.quote: We confirm that synchrotron radiation is mostly responsible for the continuum emission from AGNs at $\sim 1.4$–300 GHz.
